methodologyNotes: The roster covers 12 USB and PCIe video capture cards for streaming/recording spanning 2018-2024, sourced from official manufacturer product and spec pages (elgato.com, avermedia.com, razer.com, magewell.com), official Corsair/AVerMedia/Razer press releases, and corroborated by major retail listings (Amazon, Best Buy, B&H Photo Video, Micro Center) and tech-review coverage (TechPowerUp, Windows Central, HotHardware, PC Gamer). Prices are published US MSRP/launch price or dominant current retail; null is used for any spec that could not be confirmed from a primary or reliable secondary source. Boolean true/false is used for HDR and VRR support; null means not documented. max_capture_resolution/framerate refer to the maximum hardware/host capture the device records, NOT passthrough (an important distinction: many devices passthrough far higher resolutions than they capture). Adversarial re-verification on 2026-06-20 corrected 6 of 12 records: 4 wrong prices, 1 fabricated passthrough number (HDMI 2.0 cannot carry 4K240), 1 mislabeled encoding type, and 1 wrong release year. All 12 products were verified to exist; none were removed.

products.name: Elgato Game Capture 4K X
products.priceNote: Launch MSRP $229.99 per Corsair press release (Feb 1, 2024) and multiple retailers; elgato.com later lists $249.99
products.provenance: USB 3.2 Gen 2 interface, HDMI 2.1 passthrough up to 4K144 with HDR10/VRR, and capture up to 2160p144 (4K144) confirmed via Elgato help docs and retailer spec listings (Amazon/Best Buy/Micro Center). Launch date Feb 1, 2024 confirmed via Corsair newsroom. CORRECTED priceUsd 249.99 -> 229.99: official launch MSRP was $229.99 per Corsair press coverage (thefpsreview, eteknix) and current B&H/retailer pricing; the $249.99 on elgato.com is a later list price. Encoding is software/host-based (no onboard encode chip; UVC stream to PC).

products.name: Elgato HD60 X
products.priceNote: MSRP; widely seen at sale prices of $99-$150 in 2025-2026
products.provenance: VERIFIED unchanged. USB-C 3.2 interface, 4K60 VRR HDR10 passthrough, max capture 2160p30 (4K30) or 1080p60 HDR10, hardware H.264 encoder confirmed via Elgato supported-resolutions docs and PC Gamer/Best Buy listings. MSRP $179.99 and April 2022 launch (GlobeNewswire) confirmed.

products.name: Elgato 4K60 Pro MK.2
products.priceNote: MSRP at launch; available at ~$199 at major retailers in 2025-2026
products.provenance: Launch Aug 20, 2019 (Gamescom) and MSRP $249.99 confirmed via Corsair press release and TechPowerUp. PCIe 2.0 x4, HDMI 2.0 in/out, 4K60 HDR10 capture confirmed. CORRECTED max_passthrough '4K240 / 1440p144 / 1080p240' -> '4K60 / 1440p144 / 1080p240': the device uses HDMI 2.0, which physically cannot carry 4K240; official Elgato spec lists passthrough max 2160p60 (4K60), with 1440p144 and 1080p240 only at lower resolutions. The original '4K240' was fabricated/impossible. VRR not supported. Onboard hardware H.264/HEVC encoder. Replaced Best Buy corroboration with TechPowerUp launch article (more durable).

products.name: Elgato Cam Link 4K
products.priceNote: MSRP $129.99; seen on sale ~$79-99 at retailers in 2025-2026
products.provenance: Camera-input capture dongle; no passthrough port -> passthrough null. Launch Nov 27, 2018 (Corsair press release) and USB 3.0 interface confirmed. Captures up to 4K30 or 1080p60 confirmed. CORRECTED priceUsd 99.99 -> 129.99: the official/established MSRP is $129.99 per TweakTown review, Micro Center, B&H and camelcamelcamel history; the $99.99 was wrong. HDR/VRR not documented for this device (UVC webcam-style device).

products.name: Elgato HD60 S+
products.priceNote: MSRP at launch; succeeded by HD60 X, available on secondary market
products.provenance: VERIFIED unchanged. Launch Sept 24, 2019 confirmed (Corsair press release, LanOC). USB 3.0 Type-C, HDMI 2.0 in/out, 4K60 HDR10 zero-lag passthrough; max capture 2160p30 (4K30) or 1080p60 HDR10 (2160p60 cannot transit USB 3.0 so it captures at 1080p60 / 4K30) confirmed via Elgato supported-resolutions doc. Onboard hardware encoder. VRR not supported (arrived with HD60 X successor). MSRP $199.99 confirmed.

products.name: AVerMedia Live Gamer 4K 2.1 (GC575)
products.priceNote: MSRP per AVerMedia; discounted to ~$230 at retailers in 2025-2026
products.provenance: Launch Jan 2024 and MSRP $269.99 confirmed via AVerMedia and retailer listings (Best Buy/Amazon/Micro Center). PCIe Gen 3 x4, HDMI 2.1 input, 4K144 passthrough with HDR/VRR, 4K60 capture confirmed. CORRECTED encoding 'hardware' -> 'software': per TechPowerUp, the GC575 is the PCIe sibling of the GC553G2 on identical hardware and outputs UNCOMPRESSED formats (NV12 4K60, YUY2/P010 4K30, RGB24 at lower res) -> it is a UVC/software-encode device; the host PC performs compression. No onboard H.264/H.265 encode chip. Replaced corroboration with TechPowerUp review (more durable than the press-release slug).

products.name: AVerMedia Live Gamer Ultra 2.1 (GC553G2)
products.priceNote: MSRP at launch; discounted to ~$200-220 at retailers in 2025-2026
products.provenance: Launch Oct 2023 confirmed (Windows Central, TechPowerUp). MSRP $299.99 confirmed from AVerMedia US shop page. USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-C, HDMI 2.1 input, 4K144 passthrough with HDR/VRR. CORRECTED max_capture_framerate 60 -> 144: the official AVerMedia shop spec lists max capture as 2160p144 on Windows (2160p60 on macOS); the true device maximum is 4K144, so the conservative '60' understated it. Software/UVC encoding (outputs YUY2, NV12, RGB24, P010, MJPEG; host PC encodes) confirmed.

products.name: AVerMedia Live Gamer MINI (GC311)
products.priceNote: MSRP at launch; widely available under $100 by 2025
products.provenance: VERIFIED unchanged. USB 2.0 Micro interface, HDMI in/passthrough at max 1080p60, onboard hardware H.264 encoder, no HDR/VRR support confirmed via AVerMedia page and CGMagazine/PC Gamer reviews. MSRP ~$129.99 and 2019 release confirmed. Replaced KitGuru corroboration with CGMagazine review (cited in original provenance, more reliably reachable). No 4K or HDR capability.

products.name: AVerMedia Live Gamer Portable 2 Plus (GC513)
products.provenance: USB interface, 4K60 lag-less passthrough, 1080p60 capture, onboard hardware encoder, standalone PC-free microSD recording confirmed via AVerMedia and Windows Central. CORRECTED priceUsd 149.99 -> 139.99: official MSRP is $139.99. CORRECTED releaseDate '2017' -> '2018-09': the GC513 was released September 16, 2018 (Windows Central review, AVerMedia), not 2017. Replaced the dead/event corroboration URL with the Windows Central review.

products.name: Razer Ripsaw HD
products.priceNote: MSRP at launch per Razer newsroom
products.provenance: VERIFIED unchanged. Launch April 11, 2019 and MSRP $159.99 confirmed via Razer newsroom and Windows Central/Tom's Guide. USB 3.0, HDMI 2.0 input, 4K60 passthrough, 1080p60 capture confirmed. HDR/VRR not documented -> null. Software/UVC encoding (host CPU/OBS); 3.5mm audio mix-in. Updated source URL to the live Razer product page (newsroom slug less stable).

products.name: Razer Ripsaw X
products.priceNote: MSRP at launch per HotHardware/XDA coverage
products.provenance: VERIFIED unchanged. Launch Sept 30, 2021 and MSRP $139.99 confirmed via HotHardware/XDA/9to5Toys. USB 3.0, HDMI 2.0 input, max capture 4K30 (or 1080p120), 4K60 passthrough confirmed via Razer support and Amazon listing. HDR/VRR not documented -> null. Software/UVC encoding. Designed primarily for camera capture (DSLR/mirrorless).

products.name: Magewell USB Capture HDMI 4K Plus
products.priceNote: Current US retail $545 (B&H, Proflixsales); pro broadcast-grade pricing
products.provenance: Specs confirmed: USB 3.0 (USB 3.1 Gen 1) interface, HDMI 2.0 DCI 4K input up to 4096x2160p60 with loop-through, capture up to 4096x2160p30 (and 1080p90); FPGA-based signal processing delivered as a UVC stream (host encodes -> software). HDR/VRR not documented -> null. CORRECTED priceUsd 479 -> 545: the dominant published US retail is $545 (B&H Photo Video and Proflixsales); the $479 was a low reseller outlier. Release date not published by Magewell -> null. Professional broadcast device, not a gaming-specific card. Replaced tech-specs corroboration with the Amazon listing that explicitly states 'Up to 4K60 Input, Up to 4K30 Capture'.
